chunks.title: Description
chunks.text: The HP-40 pump supplies hydraulic pressure to the landing gear and the flight controls. An electric motor turns the pump. The pump is in the left wheel well.

chunks.title: Pressure limits
chunks.text: The normal system pressure is 3000 psi. Do not let the pressure go above 3200 psi. The relief valve opens at 3250 psi.

chunks.title: Filter
chunks.text: Replace the filter element every 600 flight hours. Replace it before this time if the clog indicator shows red.

chunks.title: Fluid temperature
chunks.text: High fluid temperature stops the pump automatically. The limit is 120 °C. Let the fluid cool before you start the pump again.

chunks.title: Approved fluid
chunks.text: Use only fluid that meets the standard MIL-PRF-83282. Do not mix two types of fluid. The list of approved fluids is in Section 12.

chunks.title: Before maintenance
chunks.text: Set the pump switch to OFF before maintenance. Release the system pressure with the bleed valve. Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag to the switch.

chunks.title: Seal and cover
chunks.text: Replace the shaft seal at each overhaul. Apply grease to the new seal before you install it. The torque of the cover bolts is 8 Nm.

chunks.title: Accumulator
chunks.text: The accumulator keeps pressure in the system when the pump stops. Its nitrogen precharge is 1200 psi. Check the precharge every 300 flight hours.

chunks.title: Dry running
chunks.text: Do not operate the pump without fluid. After 30 seconds without fluid, the pump bearings become hot and fail.

chunks.title: Pump noise
chunks.text: A loud noise from the pump can show air in the fluid. Bleed the system to remove the air.

chunks.title: Leak check
chunks.text: Look for leaks at the pump fittings after each flight. Report a leak to maintenance immediately.

chunks.title: Motor current
chunks.text: The motor current is 40 A at normal pressure. A current above 55 A shows a worn pump.
